# Independent audit: arithmetic zero/positive parity and zero-fiber descent

Source: `candidate 64170809f2768d34`.

**Full Sections 1–5 PASS.** No correction requested. The exact checker was
independently rerun with the workspace math runtime: **10,317 checks PASS**.

## Anchored equality, quantiles and parity

The jointly concave root (L^{1/N}(E^{1/d})^{d/N}\) remains well defined
and concave when (L\) has zeros. Formed marks in anchored relations are
own-interior because each input has an own ball. An attained proper cap
at the formed mark has a strictly decreasing tail immediately to the
right of its threshold. Monotonicity then excludes every later plateau
at the same mass. Hence its threshold is exactly the right mass quantile,
and all endpoint thresholds are at most that value. Concavity yields
the reverse weighted inequality, forcing equality throughout.

The Holder argument with zero and positive inputs is strictly stronger:
the omitted zero-(L\) inputs still have positive energy root, so adding
their terms in the second Holder factor strictly increases the lower
bound. This proves mixed zero/positive anchored inputs impossible. A
nonnegative concave function with an interior zero vanishes throughout
that own fiber. Thus zero and positive statuses cannot coexist at one
base. Forming sampled barycenters proves each status set closed; lattice
completeness makes the same-parity midpoint available and proves their
parity sets disjoint. No mass exhaustion is inferred.

## Uniform small-buffer properness

The nonnegative concave superlevel homothety proves the sampled maximum
bound (\max L\le NM/V_p\); this gives (f\le N^{1/N}\) uniformly over
all parameters. The actual continuous strip bound therefore controls
depth error uniformly. Ordinary depth is zero on each own boundary and
has a positive maximum, so maximizing marks stay uniformly interior.

The atomic gap (D_0(p,y)\le\operatorname{baseDepth}(p)-V_p/2\) is
legitimate: a generic minimizing base normal avoids all other base
points, and a sufficiently large finite tilt preserves those strict
statuses while selecting an own cap of mass at most (V_p/2\). The
rank-zero convention follows from opposite continuous cuts. Small
buffer error preserves a uniform gap.

The fixed finite-base threshold clamp retains the actual cap masses
and gives bounded base coefficients, so the nonvertical infimum is
attained. A cap capturing the whole own fiber has mass at least base
depth: otherwise the bases of fibers not wholly captured would have
the source in their convex hull, and convexly combining a missed point
from each would contradict full own capture. The attained cap therefore
is not full; because it contains an own-interior source, it is proper.
This proves the stated local strictness without a global tail assertion
or a regularity assumption on other fibers.

## Actual interval deformation and exact normalized derivative

For lengths ((a,1,1)\), the source supporting-majorant proof extends
to every full-space concave parameter, not just affine ones. Nonnegative
values at the two left endpoints give
(b\le\ell-a|c|/2\), and the actual mean gives
(L(0,0)\ge(a+2)/3\). Equality forces the unique stated affine
representative. The exact endpoint-tail clipping and finite isolating
tilts check every continuous orientation and base tilt. All endpoint
and pure-base gaps remain strict on the stated parameter interval.

The two ambient inequalities defining the path shrink exactly the left
sampled interval, leave the other two fixed, and remain convex and
nested at every real base. The removed parameter integral is exactly
zero. Arithmetic renormalization is thus multiplication by (M_t/M\),
as stated; covariance still changes and has been retained.

Independently differentiating
(D^2=(a^3+2)/(36(a+2))\) gives

\[
 (a+2)D'-D
 =\frac32D\left(\frac{a^2(a+2)}{a^3+2}-1\right),
\]

which reproduces the displayed derivative. Since (D\le1/6\), its
strict positive lower bound follows without assuming a sign for the
parenthesized fraction. Decreasing (a\) therefore strictly lowers the
actual globally optimized normalized buffered value.

The final scope is correct: this excludes the specified centered
three-interval zero optimum from joint body minimality. It does not
exclude arbitrary zero fibers or zero boundary faces, and it does not
silently transfer logarithmic normalization's amplified zero-cut gain.
